name: The Night Watchman
role: Keeps the watch book — and tells you only what is different from normal
greet.4: Hear, you people, and let me tell you …
fit.yes: Every server can use a watch at night. His first round notes what is normal.
fire_note: Nothing keeps running: his rounds stop. His watch book stays — hired again, he takes a fresh look at what is normal.
bubble.first: My first round is still to come. Then I note what is normal.

bubble.open.one: One entry you don't know yet.

round_now_title: Walk a round right away instead of waiting for the next one
round_failed: The round went wrong — the messenger's log says why.
round.title: The last round
round.sub: Every five minutes, also with the office closed. He only reads what lives in RAM or on the flash — no disk wakes up.
round.first: His first round records what is normal now — nothing is reported for it.
round.failed: The last round went wrong — the messenger's log says why. He tries again at the next one.
round.skipped: The syslog grew by more than {size} since the round before — he read the newest part only.
round.no_docker: Docker didn't answer on the last round — containers were left out.
round.no_shares: Unraid's list of shares wasn't there on the last round — shares were left out.
book.title: Watch book
book.sub: What was different from normal, newest first. «I know, thanks» makes that state the new normal — then only what changes after it is told again.
ack_title: Make this the new normal: it leaves what's open and isn't told again.
ack_all_title: Everything open in the watch book becomes the new normal

ack_all_text.one: One entry becomes the new normal: what it names (an address, rights, a plugin, a file, a share). Only what changes after that is told again.
ack_all_text.other: {n} entries become the new normal: what they name (addresses, rights, plugins, files, shares). Only what changes after that is told again.

acked_all.one: Noted — one entry is normal now.

state.open_title: Not noted yet: it counts at the team lead, on his picture and on the Dashboard
state.noted_title: You know about it: this state is normal now
state.watch_title: He took over the watch here and noted what was normal then
noted.teamlead: Noted at the team lead on {when}.
noted.baseline: Closed on {when}, when he took over the watch anew.
group_title.login: Logins to Unraid's WebGUI and by SSH, from the syslog
group_title.plugin: Installed plugins and where they take their updates from
group_title.flash: Unraid's configuration on the boot flash
group_title.share: Shares that guests reach without a password

detail.unknown.one: one name that is no user here
detail.unknown.other: {n} names that are no users here

detail.name: Container
detail.not_told: Waiting to be told: per kind one notification an hour at most.
detail.book_only: Only in the watch book — this kind doesn't go to Unraid's notifications.
entry.login_new_ip: Login from a new address: {user} from {ip} — {service}
entry.share_public: {share} is now open to guests over {proto}
entry.watch: Took over the watch. Normal now: {ips} login addresses, {containers} containers ({special} with special rights), {plugins} plugins, {shares} shares ({open} open to guests).

adopt.login_failures: «I know, thanks»: failures from this address are only counted from then on, no longer reported.
adopt.container_new: «I know, thanks»: the container with these rights is normal.
adopt.container_privileged: «I know, thanks»: running privileged is normal for this container.
adopt.container_host: «I know, thanks»: using the host directly is normal for this container.
adopt.container_ports: «I know, thanks»: these ports are normal for this container.
adopt.container_rights: «I know, thanks»: these rights are normal for this container.
adopt.plugin_new: «I know, thanks»: the plugin and its source are normal.
adopt.plugin_source: «I know, thanks»: the new source is normal.
adopt.flash_go: «I know, thanks»: go as it is now is normal.
adopt.flash_extra: «I know, thanks»: the file as it is now is normal.
adopt.flash_user: «I know, thanks»: the user is normal.
adopt.flash_password: «I know, thanks»: the new password is normal.
adopt.flash_ssh_key: «I know, thanks»: the key is normal.

check.quiet: The night watchman's watch book has nothing open
check.quiet_how: Whatever he finds different from normal shows up here until you note it on his page.

check.login_new_ip.one: Login from a new address: {user} from {ip} ({service})
check.login_new_ip.other: {n} logins from new addresses, the newest: {user} from {ip} ({service})

check.login_new_ip_how: If that was you (a new device, a VPN), «I know, thanks» on the night watchman's page adds the address to the known ones. If not: change root's password and check who can reach the server from outside (Settings → Management Access, port forwardings on your router).

check.login_failures.other: Failed logins from {n} addresses, the newest: {ip} ({service})

check.login_failures_how: Someone tried to log in and failed again and again. A device of yours with an old password? Correct it there. An address from outside: the server can be reached from the internet — close the port forwarding or put a VPN in front. Unraid locks the WebGUI login of an address for 15 minutes after three failures.

check.container_new.other: {n} new containers with special rights, the newest: {name} ({rights})

check.container_new_how: A container with such rights reaches deep into the server. Installed on purpose: note it on the night watchman's page. If not: look at it under Docker and remove it.

check.container_privileged.other: {n} containers now run privileged, the newest: {name}

check.container_privileged_how: A privileged container can do nearly anything on the server. Switched on yourself (Docker → the container → Edit → Privileged): note it. If not: switch it off again.

check.container_host.other: {n} containers now use the host directly, the newest: {name} ({rights})

check.container_host_how: With the host's network or processes a container sees the server itself. Intended: note it. If not: set its network type back under Docker → the container → Edit.

check.container_ports.other: {n} containers publish new ports, the newest: {name} ({rights})

check.container_ports_how: New ports make the app reachable in your network — and from outside through a port forwarding. Intended: note it.

check.container_rights.other: {n} containers have new rights, the newest: {name} ({rights})

check.container_rights_how: Capabilities, devices or the Docker socket give a container more power over the server. Intended: note it. If not: remove them under Docker → the container → Edit.
check.plugin_new_how: A plugin runs as root on the server. Installed it yourself: note it on the night watchman's page. If not: remove it under Plugins.

check.plugin_source.other: {n} plugins update from somewhere else now, the newest: {name} from {source}

check.plugin_source_how: The plugin takes its updates from another place now — usually the author moved. Check that it is still the same project, then note it.
check.flash_go_how: /boot/config/go runs as root at every start of the server. Changed it yourself: note it. If not: look at it in a terminal (the night watchman never reads its text).

check.flash_extra.one: A file in /boot/extra is new or changed: {file}
check.flash_extra.other: {n} files in /boot/extra are new or changed, the newest: {file}

check.flash_extra_how: Packages in /boot/extra are installed at every start of the server. Put there by you: note it. If not: remove it.

check.flash_user.other: {n} new users on the flash, the newest: {user}

check.flash_user_how: Users are added under Users. Added yourself: note it. If not: remove the user.
check.flash_password_how: Changed it yourself (Users): note it. If not: set a new password for this user right away.

check.flash_ssh_key.other: {n} new SSH keys, the newest for {user}: {key}

check.flash_ssh_key_how: A key lets its owner log in by SSH without a password. Yours: note it. If not: remove it under Users → the user → SSH authorized keys.

check.share_public.one: {share} is now open to guests over {proto}
check.share_public.other: {n} shares are now open to guests, the newest: {share} over {proto}

check.share_public_how: Guests reach it without a password. Intended: note it. If not: set the share's security to Private (Shares → the share → SMB Security Settings or NFS Security Settings).

notify.footer: The night watchman keeps all of it in his watch book in the office. «I know, thanks» there makes it the new normal.
watch.title: What I keep an eye on
watch.sub: What is normal: what he saw when he took over the watch, and what you noted since. What gets safer (fewer rights, a share closed) becomes normal by itself.
watch.none: He records it on his first round.

watch.fail_ips_sum.one: one address — its failures are only counted
watch.fail_ips_sum.other: {n} addresses — their failures are only counted

watch.containers_wait: Docker wasn't running when he took over — he learns the containers on the next round Docker answers.

watch.go_lines.one: one line — he keeps only a fingerprint of it
watch.go_lines.other: {n} lines — he keeps only fingerprints of them

watch.shares_none: none — every share needs a login
watch.shares_wait: Unraid's list of shares wasn't there when he took over — he learns it on the next round.
help.book_text: Every entry is something that was different from normal: when, what, from where. A row unfolds to its details. «new» counts at the team lead, on his picture and on Unraid's Dashboard until you note it; the book keeps the last {keep} entries, noted ones for {days} days.
help.ack_text: Makes the state the entry names the new normal — the address joins the known ones, the container keeps its rights, the plugin its source. Then only what changes after it is told again. «I know, thanks» on his finding at the team lead counts here too.
help.normal_text: On his first round after hiring he records what is there and reports nothing for it — also the login addresses in the syslog. Hired again later, he takes a fresh look.
help.round_text: Every five minutes in the background, also with the office closed. «A round now» doesn't wait.
help.logins_text: WebGUI and SSH logins from the syslog: a login from an address he hasn't seen yet; {burst} or more failed logins from one address within {minutes} minutes. He keeps the names tried only when they are users of this server — somebody may have typed a password into the name field.
help.containers_text: Newly privileged, the host's network or processes, new ports, capabilities, devices, the Docker socket or the whole server mounted — shown as the flags of docker run. A new container only counts when it has such rights.
help.plugins_text: A new plugin, or one that takes its updates from another place now (the host; on GitHub and the like also the owner).
help.flash_text: /boot/config/go, files in /boot/extra, users, changed passwords and SSH keys. Of go he keeps fingerprints of the lines, of passwords only a fingerprint of each — never the text.
help.shares_text: A share (also a disk, a pool or the flash) that guests now reach without a password, over SMB or NFS — as Unraid applies it.
help.notify_text: Important kinds go to Unraid's notifications right away (the bell, mail or push): per kind one message an hour at most, so a burst gives one. New ports and capabilities only go into the book.
help.safe_text: He changes nothing on the server and reads only what lives in RAM or on the flash — no disk wakes up. Not Fix Common Problems' checks ("SSH is on"): only what changed.
fact.quiet: Nothing open in the watch book
errors.watch_busy: The watch book is busy just now — try again in a moment.
errors.watch_gone: That entry isn't open any more — perhaps it was noted in another browser.
errors.watch_start_failed: The round could not be started — the messenger's log says why.
